title: Stochastic warmup gridwalk - microbenchmark log
content:
Context: quick exploratory run to see whether mixing deterministic prewarm (sequential prefix loading) with stochastic prefetch (randomized KV priming across likely prefixes) reduces p99 spikes under bursty arrival patterns. Notes to self: this is a noisy domain — keep seed + full traces.

Hypothesis: deterministic prewarm avoids cold path for hot prefixes but fails when arrival clusters shift; stochastic priming spreads KV cache coverage and may reduce worst-case tail for short bursts at cost of slightly higher average latency.

Environment:
- infra: dedicated dev-GPU pool (2x A100 80GB equivalent) under lightweight overcommit (30% background noise).
- model: open-variant v1 13B (float16, KV cache enabled).
- runtime: local branch warmup/gridwalk-experiments (PR 987).
- batch size: per-request single-token streaming (simulating chat-turn inference).
- seq len: 512 typical, 1024 max in some runs.
- load generator: internal qps-replay tool, with mixed poisson+burst arrivals.
- seed: 87421 (recorded trace).

Experiment matrix (gridwalk): two axes: prewarm mode = {none, deterministic-prefix, stochastic-prime-0.1, stochastic-prime-0.3, hybrid-1} and arrival pattern = {steady-50qps, burst-200qps-10s, staircase-10->150}. Each run 600s, collect p50/p95/p99, qps achieved, error rate. Keep TTL cache eviction = default 30m.

Raw summary table (aggregated across 3 replicas; numbers in ms unless noted):
config,p50,p95,p99,qps,error_rate
none_steady-50,32,67,154,49.2,0.01%
deterministic-prefix_steady-50,29,61,142,49.5,0.005%
stochastic-0.1_steady-50,31,63,128,49.3,0.004%
stochastic-0.3_steady-50,33,66,121,49.1,0.006%
hybrid-1_steady-50,30,62,119,49.4,0.003%

none_burst-200,35,180,980,180.5,0.9%
deterministic-prefix_burst-200,33,140,560,179.6,0.5%
stochastic-0.1_burst-200,34,125,320,178.8,0.3%
stochastic-0.3_burst-200,36,118,210,178.2,0.4%
hybrid-1_burst-200,32,110,165,179.1,0.2%

none_staircase,34,92,420,120.7,0.4%
deterministic-prefix_staircase,31,85,300,121.9,0.25%
stochastic-0.1_staircase,33,80,210,121.5,0.2%
stochastic-0.3_staircase,35,78,180,121.1,0.28%
hybrid-1_staircase,30,75,145,121.8,0.15%

Interpretation notes (working):
- Steady low qps: stochastic priming improves p99 modestly vs none; deterministic also helps. Differences small because cache has time to adapt.
- Bursts: deterministic-prefix reduces tail but still suffers large p99 spikes when the burst targets prefixes the prewarm didn't cover. Stochastic priming (0.1/0.3) lowers p99 more consistently; higher stochastic fraction (0.3) helps more but increases p50 slightly. Hybrid (deterministic+stochastic) gives best overall tail while preserving good median.
- Staircase ramps show similar pattern: hybrid performs best on p99 and keeps qps stable.

Interesting signal: p99 in none mode during burst had huge outliers (up to ~2.4s in raw traces). Looking at traces, these correspond to KV cache miss + model cold-start recompute combined with scheduler contention spikes during burst.

Quick charts to produce next:
- time-series p99 over run for each config (burst case) with event overlay for burst start.
- heatmap prefix-hit-rate vs time across configs.
- histogram of tail outliers (>=500ms) and stack traces sampling.

Operational takeaway (draft):
- For production workloads with unpredictable microbursts, implement a hybrid warmup policy: deterministic prewarm for top-K prefixes + stochastic priming across top-N buckets with adjustable fraction. Default fraction 0.15 seems a good middle ground; 0.3 helps strict tail SLAs but increases median slightly.
- Add adaptive controller: detect rising arrival entropy (new prefixes appearing) and increase stochastic fraction temporarily.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune eviction TTL vs priming frequency; current TTL likely too long for long-tailed prefix sets. Run TTL sweep.
- Re-run with quantized model variant (8-bit) to see if cache miss penalty changes relative advantages.
- Add mem-profiler to see whether stochastic priming causes unacceptable memory churn on Dedicated nodes.
- Correlate with scheduler logs (PR 987 touches scheduling decisions) to confirm combined effect.

Notes-to-self: push cleaned traces to S3 bucket rt-warmup/traces/2025-11-03/ (completed). Attach lightweight notebook that parses traces and reproduces table. Share with Mira for follow-up on controller design.

End.
